limitations: Pre-registration document only — no harness/campaign code is implemented here (that is milestones M0-M5, each a separate story). Claim scope is bounded per §3/§10: ledger integrity detects only accidental corruption + naive edits (adversarial re-digest is Tier-C, out of scope); determinism binds to the recorded environment; the tamper matrix is a coverage list, not a security proof.
pitfalls: 1) verification_evidence_refresh_stale re-stamps storyFilesHash freshness but does NOT re-run the command or update the recorded note — so after story-owned (doc) content changes, the note keeps asserting the OLD digest. The test-coverage lane caught this as F-004 (high). Fix: genuinely re-record via verification_evidence_add against current HEAD, do not rely on refresh_stale for content drift. 2) Any doc edit to resolve a finding changes storyFilesHash, which stales ALL review-lane passes and forces a DEV->REVIEW round restart (the gate refuses in-round re-binding) — batch every doc edit before re-review to avoid extra rounds. 3) When re-recording the content-integrity intent, refresh the scratchpad backup file to the new committed content FIRST so the digest-match holds. 4) In this harness the shell cwd intermittently resets to the parent repo between bash calls — always cd into the worktree at the top of each call. 5) A stale validation-execution-lock (dead pid) under .lattice/locks/validation blocked the first TEST validate; it auto-cleared (staleMs=120s) — just re-run validate.
